True when an autopilot text contains 'flight plan received' (any letter case): what ArduPilot sends when a ground station finishes uploading a mission.

Says whether a NAV_WAYPOINT may be uploaded: latitude, longitude and altitude must be finite numbers, the position within +-90 / +-180 degrees, and not (0, 0). It is the last safety check before the autopilot.

A small decision maker (no ROS) for WHEN waypoint_manager asks MAVROS to read the mission again: it waits a moment after a trigger, merges triggers, ignores the echo of our own upload, waits for the service, retries, and abandons a read that never gets an answer.

Sets the timings (delay_s 2 s after a trigger, own_push_quiet_s 15 s, retry_delay_s 2 s, max_attempts 3, pull_timeout_s 45 s, which is longer than MAVROS's own 30 s limit for reading a mission) and starts with nothing to do.
Asks for a pull delay_s from now. If a pull is already running, the reason is kept for one more pull afterwards; if one is already planned, the reasons are merged instead of planning a second.
Handles 'Flight plan received': ignored (returns False) when it comes within 15 s of our own upload, otherwise it plans a pull and returns True.
Handles arming: plans a pull 0.5 s from now, one last read before take-off.
Remembers the time of waypoint_manager's own mission upload (the target waypoints), which starts the 15 s quiet window.

Says what to do now: ACTION_TIMEOUT if the pull in flight has waited 45 s, ACTION_PULL if a pull is due and allowed, otherwise None. A due pull is put off to the end of the 15 s window after our own upload (MAVROS refuses a pull during a push), or by 2 s when the service is not ready.
Records that the pull request was just sent: in flight, sent at 'now', nothing else planned.
Records how the pull ended and returns 'ok', 'retry' (another try in 2 s) or 'gave_up' (after 3 failures in a row). A trigger that arrived while the pull was running is then planned.

mod:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint.explain: The waypoint_manager node. It mirrors the autopilot's mission from /mavros/mission/waypoints, publishes num_waypoints, takeoff_index, next_after_takeoff, rtl_index, last_before_rtl and buffer_wp as its own ROS parameters (only the changed ones, in one update), and serves /addWaypoint: insert a NAV_WAYPOINT (or DO_SET_SERVO) into the copy and upload the WHOLE mission with /mavros/mission/push. It asks MAVROS to re-read the mission after 'Flight plan received', when the drone is armed, and at start-up, without ever blocking.
mod:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint.how_it_fits: Started by tracker.launch.xml (package waypoint_mavros, command waypoint). Its parameters are read by the photo trigger (buffer_wp: stop the photos) and by main_controller (where to hold and where to insert targets); main_controller is its only /addWaypoint client in flight. It also serves /delWaypoint and /updateMission (not used in flight) and sends the STATUSTEXT texts 'Heartbeat established', 'Mission re-read (N items)' and 'Object waypoint reached. Holding for 3 seconds.' (over a target waypoint, whose hold time is 3 s).

fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.explain: The node class 'waypoint_manager': mission copy, index parameters and the /addWaypoint service.

Builds the node: subscribes to /mavros/state, /mavros/mission/reached, /mavros/mission/waypoints and /mavros/statustext/recv, creates the /mavros/statustext/send publisher and clients for /mavros/mission/pull, /mavros/mission/push, /mavros/mission/clear and /mavros/set_mode, offers the services /addWaypoint, /delWaypoint and /updateMission, declares the six index parameters (num_waypoints 0, the others -1), and starts the MissionRepullPolicy with a 0.5 s timer.
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.called_when: Once at start-up (from the module's main()).

fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.explain: Stores MAVROS's connected and armed flags. At the moment the drone becomes armed (not counting the very first message) it asks for a mission re-read: the last chance to pick up a mission that was uploaded without notice.

Stores the mission MAVROS publishes, works out the six indices from scratch (derive_mission_indices; runway: takeoff 1, next 2, rtl 11, last_before_rtl 10, buffer_wp 9, 12 items), logs them, and publishes only the changed ones as parameters in ONE atomic update.
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.called_when: On every /mavros/mission/waypoints message (after a pull, an upload or MAVROS start-up).
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.effects: One /parameter_events message, which makes main_controller and the photo trigger re-read their indices.

fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.explain: Would set every index back to 'not known' (num_waypoints 0, the rest -1) with six separate parameter updates. Nothing calls it.

Uploads the WHOLE mission copy to the autopilot (/mavros/mission/push, start_index 0) without waiting for the result (_on_push_done logs it), after telling the re-read policy that this upload is our own. It first waits, 1 s per try, until the push service exists.
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.effects: MAVLink mission upload to ArduPilot. ArduPilot answers 'Flight plan received', which the policy then ignores.

fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.explain: Logs how the mission upload ended ('Mission upload done: N items (M transferred)' or 'FAILED') and restarts the 15 s 'this was our own upload' quiet window from now.
Old BLOCKING mission read: calls /mavros/mission/pull and spins until MAVROS answers. Only delete_waypoint uses it; the normal re-reads use the non-blocking request_mission_pull.
Done-callback of the blocking pull: logs 'Successfully pulled N from drone.' when MAVROS reports success.

Asks for a mission re-read 'soon' without blocking: it hands the reason to the policy (arming uses a 0.5 s delay, other triggers 2 s) and logs 'Will re-read the mission from the autopilot (<reason>)'. The pull itself is sent by _repull_tick.
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.called_when: At start-up once connected, and when the drone is armed.

fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.explain: Watches the autopilot's texts. On 'Flight plan received' (a mission upload finished) it plans a re-read in 2 s, unless the text is the echo of our own target upload within the last 15 s, which it ignores.

Timer step that asks the policy what to do: send the mission pull now (call_async to /mavros/mission/pull, answer handled by _on_pull_done), abandon a pull that has had no answer for 45 s, or nothing.

Gives up on a pull MAVROS never answered: forgets and cancels the waiting request, counts it as failed, and warns that the last mission copy (N items, rtl_index R) is kept and that it will try again in 2 s (or that it gave up until the next upload or arming). The mission copy and the parameters are not touched.
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.called_when: From _repull_tick when the policy says ACTION_TIMEOUT.

fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.explain: Handles MAVROS's answer to a pull (a late answer to an abandoned pull is ignored). On success it logs 'Re-read the mission from the autopilot: N items (because ...)' and sends STATUSTEXT 'Mission re-read (N items)'; on failure it retries in 2 s, up to 3 tries, then logs an error with the manual command 'ros2 service call /mavros/mission/pull mavros_msgs/srv/WaypointPull {}'.
Meant to erase the autopilot's mission (/mavros/mission/clear), but it uses a client name that does not exist, so it only logs 'Service call failed'. Nothing calls it.

Inserts mission items into the copy and uploads the whole mission. A NAV_WAYPOINT becomes command 16, frame 3 (altitude relative to home), hold time param1 = 3 s, at the given lat / lon / alt; a DO_SET_SERVO becomes command 183 with param1 = channel and param2 = PWM. An index past the end of the list, or a NaN / infinite / (0, 0) position, puts the original list back and returns False.
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.inputs: wp_list: a list of dicts with command, index and lat / lon / alt (waypoint) or channel / pwm (servo).
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.outputs: True once the upload was sent, False if refused.

fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.explain: Re-reads the mission (blocking), deletes the item at the given index if it exists, and uploads the whole mission again.
fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.called_when: From the /delWaypoint service (not used in flight).

fn:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint_.explain: Logs 'Waypoint N reached.' and, if that item has a hold time (param1 above 0), reacts by its command: a NAV_WAYPOINT (16) sends STATUSTEXT 'Object waypoint reached. Holding for N seconds.' with N = param1 (3 for the target waypoints main_controller inserts), any other command only logs 'Loiter finished. Continuing to next waypoint.'.
Broken leftover: it calls the set_mode client the wrong way (call_async(custom_mode=...)), which would raise an error. Nothing calls it; main_controller changes modes itself.
Publishes a StatusText (severity 6, INFO) on /mavros/statustext/send for the ground station and logs it.

The /addWaypoint service: turns the request into one NAV_WAYPOINT (command 16; 0 is treated as 16) or DO_SET_SERVO (183) item and calls insert_new_waypoint. It answers success = true even when the insert was refused (the refusal is only logged), and false only if something raised.
The /delWaypoint service: deletes the item at request.index through delete_waypoint and answers success.
The /updateMission service: a placeholder that does nothing and always answers success.

Runs the node: spins until MAVROS reports connected, sends 'Heartbeat established' to the ground station, asks for the first mission read (non-blocking), then spins for ever; if spinning ever crashes it logs 'waypoint_manager crashed: <traceback>' and re-raises.
Entry point of the 'waypoint' command: starts ROS, creates WaypointManager and runs its main() method.

mod:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint.explain: A DEAD backup of waypoint.py from before the October 2026 fixes. It read the mission only once, with a blocking call, at start-up; kept old index values when a new mission had no TAKEOFF or RTL item; set the six parameters one by one; and handed its /mavros/mission/reached subscription the number 0 instead of the callback (an attribute and the method are both called waypoint_reached), which probably crashed the node at the first 'reached' message.
mod:ros2_ws/src/waypoint_mavros/waypoint.how_it_fits: Not installed (it is not a .py file) and not used; only useful to compare old and new behaviour.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/package.xml.explain: Package manifest of wp_sender: ament_python, needs rclpy, interfaces and rcl_interfaces at run time.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/package.xml.how_it_fits: main_controller imports wp_sender.parameter at run time, but main's package.xml does not list wp_sender, so both simply have to be built in the same workspace.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/resource/wp_se.explain: An empty marker file. ROS 2 installs it into share/ament_index so 'ros2 run' and 'ros2 launch' can find the package 'wp_sender' by name.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/resource/wp_se.how_it_fits: Standard ament_python plumbing; nothing to edit.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/setup.cfg.explain: Tells setuptools to put this package's runnable commands ('send_wp', 'test_param') into lib/wp_sender, the folder 'ros2 run wp_sender <command>' looks in.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/setup.py.explain: Python install script of wp_sender: installs the wp_sender library (parameter.py, param_tracking.py, waypoint_sender.py) and two test commands, 'send_wp' (waypoint_sender.main) and 'test_param' (parameter.main).
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/setup.py.how_it_fits: Both commands are commented out in tracker.launch.xml; the library part is what main_controller uses.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_asyn.explain: Test file (needs rclpy / rcl_interfaces; nothing spins). It drives AsyncParameterReader with a fake node, a fake client, fake futures and a clock moved by hand, and checks that a good read is delivered, that a read with no answer is given up after timeout_s without calling the handler (old values kept, nothing raises), that it retries and ignores a late answer, and that failing calls, incomplete answers and a raising handler are reported, not raised.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_asyn.how_it_fits: End-to-end guard of the main_controller crash fix.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_copy.explain: Standard ament template test that would check copyright headers; it is marked skip, so it never runs.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_copy.how_it_fits: Lint only, not a functional test.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_flak.explain: Standard ament template test that runs the flake8 style checker over the package. AGENTS.md lists these template lint tests as pre-existing failures, so the functional test runs leave them out.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_flak.how_it_fits: Lint only; the CI gate that can fail is 'ruff check ros2_ws/src' instead.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_para.explain: Pure test file (no ROS) for param_tracking.py: values decode to the right Python types, NOT_SET becomes None, missing answers are marked, nothing is sent before a request or while the service is missing, many requests during one read give one follow-up read, a read with no answer times out, and failures are retried after the back-off until one succeeds.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_para.how_it_fits: Guards the rules of the non-blocking reader.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/test/test_pep2.explain: Standard ament template test that runs the pep257 docstring style checker over the package; like test_flake8 it is a pre-existing failure (AGENTS.md) and is left out of the functional test runs.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/__in.explain: An empty file that makes the folder a Python package, so 'import wp_sender.<module>' works.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/para.explain: The pure-Python bookkeeping (no ROS) behind AsyncParameterReader: parameter_value_to_python turns one ROS ParameterValue into a normal Python value, decode_parameter_values pairs names with answers, and ParameterReadTracker is a tiny state machine that says when to send a read, when to give one up (5 s) and when to try again (2 s later).
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/para.how_it_fits: Used by wp_sender/parameter.py (AsyncParameterReader, and the decoding in ParameterManager); unit-tested without ROS by test/test_parameter_reader.py.

fn:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/param.explain: Turns one ROS ParameterValue into a plain Python value by its type number: 1 bool, 2 int, 3 float, 4 str, 5 bytes, 6-9 lists; 0 (not set) or an unknown type gives None.
Pairs the requested parameter names with the answer's values in the same order and returns {name: value}; a missing or unset value becomes None.
A tiny state machine (no ROS) for one remote parameter read: is a read wanted, is one in flight, when was it sent, when may we try again, how many failures in a row.
Starts idle, with timeout_s (default 5 s) and retry_delay_s (default 2 s).
Marks that a fresh read is wanted; several requests before it is sent count as one.
Says ACTION_TIMEOUT if the read in flight has had no answer for timeout_s, ACTION_SEND if a read is wanted, the service is ready and the back-off time has passed, otherwise None.
Records that a request was just sent.

Records the end of the read: a success resets the failure count; a failure (an error, an incomplete answer or a timeout) adds one and automatically wants another read after retry_delay_s, so it keeps trying until one succeeds.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/para.explain: Tools to read waypoint_manager's mission-index parameters from another node. AsyncParameterReader (for use inside a running node) sends /<node>/get_parameters with call_async, handles the answer on the caller's own executor, gives up after 5 s, keeps the caller's old values and retries every 2 s. ParameterManager is the old blocking reader, now only for command-line tools such as 'ros2 run wp_sender test_param'.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/para.how_it_fits: main_controller creates AsyncParameterReader(self, 'waypoint_manager', <5 index names>, ...) at start-up and asks again after every waypoint_manager parameter event. Calling the blocking ParameterManager.get_param inside a callback is exactly what crashed main_controller in 2 of 4 simulator runs (October 2026).

fn:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/param.explain: Reads a list of parameters of another node without ever blocking: the client and a small timer live on the caller's own node, so the answers are handled by the caller's executor (no second node, no nested spinning).

Creates a GetParameters client for '/<remote_node>/get_parameters' (for main_controller: /waypoint_manager/get_parameters) and a timer every tick_s (0.5 s) on the caller's node, with a ParameterReadTracker using timeout_s 5 s and retry_delay_s 2 s.
fn:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/param.inputs: node, remote_node, names (parameter names read together), on_values (a function called with a dict after each complete read).

fn:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/param.explain: Read-only property: how many reads have failed in a row (0 after a success).
Asks for a fresh read (remembering why, for the log) and checks right away whether it can be sent; many calls during one read give one extra read.
Returns the monotonic clock in seconds (it never jumps when the wall clock is changed).
Returns the owning node's logger.
Does what the tracker says: send the request; or abandon one that took too long (cancel it, count a failure, log); or log once that it is waiting for the service to appear.
fn:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/param.called_when: Every 0.5 s (timer) and right after request().

fn:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/param.explain: Sends the GetParameters request with call_async and attaches _on_done; if sending itself fails it counts a failure and logs it.

Handles the answer on the caller's executor: ignores late answers to abandoned requests and cancellations, decodes the values, counts a failure if any name has no value, otherwise logs a recovery note ('... again after N failed attempt(s)') if needed and calls on_values(values). An error inside the caller's handler is logged, never raised.

Warns 'Could not read ... Keeping the previous values; trying again in 2 s (failure N in a row).' for the first 3 failures and then only every 10th, so a missing waypoint_manager cannot flood the log.
The old BLOCKING parameter reader, a separate node: for command-line tools only, never inside a callback.
Creates the node with a unique name (parameter_manager_<process id>, so two copies never clash) and a client for waypoint_manager/get_parameters, then waits for it.
Waits for waypoint_manager/get_parameters, 1 s per try, at most 30 s; returns False if it gave up.
Reads the named parameters and BLOCKS (spins) up to 10 s for the answer; returns {name: value}, or None on a timeout or an error.
The 'test_param' command: reads waypoint_manager's five mission indices once with ParameterManager and prints them.

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/para.explain: A DEAD backup of the original parameter.py: one blocking ParameterManager node with the fixed name 'parameter_manager', a wait for the service with no limit, and spin_until_future_complete with no timeout.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/para.how_it_fits: Not used; it shows the version that could hang or crash a node (see AsyncParameterReader for the fix).

mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/wayp.explain: A command-line test client (command 'send_wp', node waypoint_client) for waypoint_manager's services. Its main() inserts a test NAV_WAYPOINT at latitude 10.5, longitude 30.2, altitude 4.2 m at index 0 through /addWaypoint, then deletes index 0 through /delWaypoint, and prints both answers.
mod:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/wayp.how_it_fits: Not launched (commented out in tracker.launch.xml). waypoint_manager uploads the whole mission after each change, so running it next to a real drone or a running simulator would rewrite the live mission twice: use it only on a bench.

fn:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/waypo.explain: Test client node 'waypoint_client' for waypoint_manager's /addWaypoint and /delWaypoint services.
Creates the /addWaypoint and /delWaypoint clients and waits until both services exist.
Waits, 1 s per try with no limit, until /addWaypoint and /delWaypoint are available.
Inserts a NAV_WAYPOINT (command 16) at the given lat, lon, alt and index through /addWaypoint, blocks until the answer arrives, and returns it.
Inserts a DO_SET_SERVO mission item (command 183, channel, pwm) at the given index through /addWaypoint and returns the answer. main() does not use it.
Deletes the mission item at the given index through /delWaypoint, blocks until the answer arrives, and returns it.
The 'send_wp' command: inserts a test waypoint (lat 10.5, lon 30.2, alt 4.2, index 0), prints the answer, deletes index 0, prints that answer, and exits.
fn:ros2_ws/src/wp_sender/wp_sender/waypo.effects: Each call makes waypoint_manager upload the whole mission to the autopilot.
